title: What does unmodelled tangential (decentring) lens distortion cost a self-calibrating bundle adjustment?
lede: a tangential coefficient p1 = 0.01 (p2 = -0.008) set to zero raises the surface error from 0.0018 to 0.0041 object radii on the wide rig (0.0020 on the narrow one) and leaks into the fitted k2; fitting p1, p2 recovers them and removes the cost. Synthetic only
summary: Takes the next step of sensing-bapp. Images are rendered with Brown–Conrady tangential coefficients p1, p2 from 0 to 0.02; one adjustment sets them to zero, the other fits them, both with focal length, k1, k2, poses and points free. On the wide rig (distance 2) p1 = 0.01 raises the surface error from 0.0018 to 0.0041 object radii (0.0077 at 0.02); on the narrow rig it is 0.0015 to 0.0020, but the held k2 there is pulled from −0.16 to +0.45 at 0.02. Fitting recovers the coefficients (0.0086 and −0.0080 for 0.0100 and −0.0080) and holds the error flat; at 2 px of noise the benefit is gone. Limits: synthetic, coefficients swept not measured, principal point at centre, one camera, correct matches, 8 seeds.
